reasons: The build model step is a placeholder that only shows an alert.
Several AI results are inserted as raw HTML without escaping.
Some step failures are only logged and not shown to the user.
No tests or example runs are visible in this packet.
The server side that answers these requests was not provided, so it could not be checked.

terms.meaning: the language that describes what a web page contains, such as text boxes and buttons
the style rules that control colors, spacing, and layout on a web page
the programming language that makes the page respond to clicks and fetch data
a specific web address on the server that the page asks for data, such as the one that generates questions
the stored collection of everything gathered so far, such as the company name and answers
converting text so that the browser shows it as plain words instead of running it as page code

depends_on: Google Fonts (external stylesheet for the Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts)
Server routes under /api/agents/ (questionnaire, comparables), not included in this packet
used_by: Not visible in this packet. The page is opened directly in the browser.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page basics and color theme
sections.what: Sets the page title, loads the fonts, and defines the dark color scheme. It also makes the top bar stay in place while the page scrolls.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps a consistent dark look across the whole page.
sections.watch_out: Colors are defined once in a shared set of settings, so changing one value changes every part of the page that uses it.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Header and main two-column layout
sections.what: Styles the top bar with the logo and a status line, and the main grid with the workflow on the left and the agent panel on the right. It also gives cards their basic look.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the steps on the left and the live agent log on the right so both are visible together.
sections.watch_out: The grid uses a fixed-width right column, so narrow screens depend on the responsive rule near the end of the file.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Form fields and card titles
sections.what: Styles the company name box, the description box, and section titles. A focused field gets a green glow so the user can see where they are typing.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes inputs easy to read and shows which field is active.
sections.watch_out: These form styles also apply to the answer boxes that are created later, so changing them changes those boxes too.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Button and spinner styles
sections.what: Defines the green primary buttons, grey secondary buttons, the dimmed look for disabled buttons, and the spinning indicator shown while work runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which action is the main one and when a step is busy.
sections.watch_out: The spinner and button styles are matched by class name, so the class names in the script must match these exactly.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Question and classification card styles
sections.what: Styles each discovery question with its explanation, and the grid of classification tiles that show industry, business model, stage, and confidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes each question easy to scan and the classification results easy to compare.
sections.watch_out: The question text comes from the server and is placed on the page as raw HTML, so styles alone do not protect against unexpected content.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Comparable company and agent panel styles
sections.what: Styles each comparable company card with name, ticker badge, similarity score, and reason. It also styles the right-side agent panel, which stays in view while the user scrolls.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the live agent status visible during long pages.
sections.watch_out: The agent panel has a height based on the window size, so it may look cramped on short screens.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Agent log entry styles
sections.what: Styles the scrolling activity log. Prompt entries are blue, success entries are green, and error entries are red.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user tell the kind of each log line at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Colors are picked by a class name the script sets, so a mistyped class name leaves the entry in the default green.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Reasoning, prompt box, and metric styles
sections.what: Styles purple reasoning entries, the boxed and scrollable view of full AI prompts, and metric tiles for key numbers.
sections.why: Likely reason: prompts are long, so they need a scrollable monospace box to be readable.
sections.watch_out: The metric tile styles are defined here, but the code in this file does not use them, so they may be unused.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Collapsible sections and small-screen layout
sections.what: Styles panels that open and close, and switches the page to a single column on screens narrower than 1200 pixels.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets long details be hidden and keeps the page usable on smaller screens.
sections.watch_out: Collapsible content has a maximum height of 2000 pixels, so anything taller is cut off. The script in this file does not appear to use these panels.

sections.name: File setup (part 10)
sections.title: Hidden class and status message styles
sections.what: Provides a class that hides any element, and styled success and error message boxes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the script shows and hides whole steps by adding or removing the hidden class.
sections.watch_out: The hidden class is marked as overriding other display rules, so new display rules can conflict with it.

sections.name: File setup (part 11)
sections.title: Steps 1 to 3 page markup
sections.what: Lays out step 1, where the user enters the company and description, step 2, where questions and answer boxes appear, and step 3, where classification and comparable companies are shown, with their buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: the workflow is split into numbered steps that are shown one at a time.
sections.watch_out: The script finds steps by their IDs (step1 to step4), so those IDs must not change.

sections.name: File setup (part 12)
sections.title: Step 4 and agent side panel markup
sections.what: Holds the financial analysis area with benchmarks and required inputs, the build model button, and the right-side status panel with the initial list of four agents.
sections.why: Likely reason: the last step shows analysis results before the model is built.
sections.watch_out: The build model button only shows a placeholder alert, so it does not build a model yet.

sections.name: File setup (part 13)
sections.title: Script state and starting discovery
sections.what: Sets up the state object that holds everything gathered so far, runs an initial log message on page load, and starts discovery. Discovery checks that a company name was typed, then sends it and the optional description to the server.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared state object lets each later step read what earlier steps produced.
sections.watch_out: The state object is also reset in startOver, so any new field must be added in both places or it will not clear.

sections.name: File setup (part 14)
sections.title: Showing discovery questions
sections.what: On success, saves the questions, logs the AI's reasoning and the number of questions, and builds one card per question with an answer box. Then it moves the user to step 2. On failure it logs an error and shows an alert.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Answer boxes are named from the question ID, or from the position if no ID exists, so repeated IDs could send answers to the wrong box.

sections.name: File setup (part 15)
sections.title: Checking and sending answers
sections.what: Collects every answer, stops and shows a message if any are blank, then sends the questions and answers to the server for classification.
sections.why: Likely reason: classification needs complete answers to be accurate.
sections.watch_out: The only check is that an answer is not blank, so a meaningless answer still passes.

sections.name: File setup (part 16)
sections.title: Showing the company classification
sections.what: Shows six tiles for industry, sub-industry, business model, revenue model, stage, and confidence. Then it adds the key insights as a list.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user a summary to check before the model is built.
sections.watch_out: The values come from the AI response and are placed on the page as raw HTML, so odd text could break the display.

sections.name: File setup (part 17)
sections.title: Modeling approach and comparables search
sections.what: Shows the recommended modeling approach text, then asks the server for comparable public companies based on industry and business model.
sections.why: Likely reason: comparable companies are used to guide the model's assumptions.
sections.watch_out: If the comparables search fails, the error is only written to the log, so the user may see an empty list without a clear reason.

sections.name: File setup (part 18)
sections.title: Showing comparable companies
sections.what: Builds one card for each comparable company with its name, ticker, similarity percentage, and reason. If none were found, it shows a short message instead.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Names and reasons are placed on the page as raw HTML, and a missing similarity score is shown as zero percent.

sections.name: File setup (part 19)
sections.title: Analyzing comparables and moving to step 4
sections.what: Sends the comparable companies for financial analysis, then asks for industry benchmarks. Once both finish, it moves the user to step 4. On failure it shows an alert and restores the button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the next step needs finished analysis data.
sections.watch_out: The benchmark step logs its own errors and does not stop the move to step 4, so the user can reach step 4 with no benchmarks.

sections.name: File setup (part 20)
sections.title: Showing benchmarks and required inputs
sections.what: Shows the benchmark results and asks the server which financial inputs the model will need. Both are displayed as raw data text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the user should know what data is needed before building the model.
sections.watch_out: Results are shown as raw JSON rather than a table, which is hard for a non-programmer to read. Errors here are only logged.

sections.name: File setup (part 21)
sections.title: Build model placeholder and navigation
sections.what: The build model button only shows an alert saying the builder is coming. The back button returns to an earlier step, and start over clears the saved data and returns to step 1.
sections.why: Likely reason: the build step is not finished, so it only announces itself.
sections.watch_out: Start over clears the saved data and inputs but not the activity log, so old log entries remain on screen.

sections.name: File setup (part 22)
sections.title: Activity log and helper functions
sections.what: Adds timestamped entries to the activity log in color, adds full AI prompts with safe escaping, updates the status line, and starts the page setup on load.
sections.why: Likely reason: the log lets the user see what each AI agent was asked and what it returned.
sections.watch_out: The agent log puts its messages on the page as raw HTML, while the prompt log escapes them, so messages with outside text could change the layout.

summary: An older, longer version of the Financial Modeling AI web page that walks the user through company discovery, questions, classification, comparable companies, benchmarks, and required inputs, with a live log of what each AI agent did.
purpose: Lets a user type a company name, answer AI-generated questions, review the AI's classification and comparable companies, and see the benchmarks and inputs it needs before building a financial model.
why: Likely reason: the page is split into numbered steps so the user checks each AI result before the next step. The side panel shows the prompts and reasoning so the user can judge the AI's work.
how: First, the page loads its styles and layout. The user enters a company name and optional description, then clicks start discovery. The page asks the server for questions and shows them one at a time. After the user answers all of them, the page sends the answers for classification, then looks up comparable companies. Next it asks for financial analysis and industry benchmarks, then for the required inputs. Every AI prompt and reply is written to the side log. The build model button only shows a placeholder message.
inputs: Typed company name, optional description, and written answers to each question. These are sent to server routes under /api/agents/ (questionnaire, comparables). The server code is not in this packet.
outputs: Question cards, a classification summary with key insights and a modeling approach, comparable company cards, benchmark data shown as raw text, a list of required inputs shown as raw text, and a running log with full prompts.
risks: The build model step is not finished and only shows an alert. Several AI results are placed on the page as raw HTML, so unexpected text could break the display or insert markup. Some failures only write to the log, so the user can move on without seeing a clear error. Benchmark and input results are raw JSON, which is hard for a non-programmer to read.
debug: Open the browser developer console and check for failed requests to the /api/agents/ routes. Check the side log first, because each step writes its prompts and errors there. If a step seems to skip, look at the matching function (for example findComparables, synthesizeBenchmarks, or determineRequiredInputs), since those catch errors and only log them. If the start over button leaves old data, check that the state object is reset in startOver.
